subject: Retention & Deletion evidence request — scope walkthrough
messages:
From: Lydia Park <lydia.park@finsight.io>
To: ava_chen <ava.chen@redwood.ai>
Cc: LegalOps <legal@finsight.io>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Evidence request: retention & deletion - SOC 2 prep

Hi Ava,

We're kicking off our SOC 2 readiness review and need a focused evidence packet around retention, residency, and deletion controls for the Redwood integration (FinSight customer tenancy). To scope this correctly, can you provide the following by next week if possible:

- Your data residency mapping for tenant data (which regions data can reside in by service component).
- Retention policy excerpts and the TTL enforcement mechanics for primary tokens and derived artifacts (embeddings, KV caches).
- Sample deletion logs showing a customer-initiated erasure flow (timestamped, who/what initiated deletion, service components touched).
- A short description of permanent vs reversible deletion paths and any archival/backup windows.

If some items require limited-access exports or tooling, happy to accept redacted samples (IDs hashed). Also confirm the point of contact for technical follow-ups (we may need a small sample export).

Thanks,
Lydia Park
Senior Compliance Manager, FinSight Analytics

From: ava_chen <ava.chen@redwood.ai>
To: Lydia Park <lydia.park@finsight.io>
Cc: ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 11:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Evidence request: retention & deletion - SOC 2 prep

Hi Lydia — thanks for the clear list. We're happy to assemble an evidence bundle. Quick clarifying Qs so we scope exactly:

1) Scope: Is this limited to production tenant data for FinSight (customer IDs in your account) or do you also need staging/test environment artifacts?
2) Time range: sample deletion logs — do you want a rolling 30-day window or a specific interval (e.g., Nov 1–15)?
3) Redaction standard: hashed IDs are fine; do you need one-way SHA256 salts or plain SHA256 will suffice for your auditors?

Planned owners: Ben (security infra) will pull logs and the TTL snippet; I'll compile policy excerpts and residency matrix. We can deliver redacted samples and a short write-up explaining lifecycle semantics.

Target ETA: confirm scope today and we can aim to deliver the first bundle by Tue, 2026-11-30. If you need DocuSign for an NDA/MAP signature, send the link and we'll expedite.

Best,
Ava Chen
Director, Compliance & GTM Security
Redwood Inference

From: ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: ava_chen <ava.chen@redwood.ai>, Lydia Park <lydia.park@finsight.io>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 19 Nov 2026 08:27:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Evidence request: retention & deletion - SOC 2 prep

Lydia/Ava — quick technical notes:

- Residency: We tag tenant objects at write time with region metadata (region_code) and maintain replication policy per model/service. We'll include the CSV export with fields: tenant_id_hash, service_component, primary_region, replica_regions, retention_ttl_days.

- TTL enforcement: our scheduler runs TTL sweeps every 24h and triggers component-specific deletion handlers (embedding-store, kv-cache, event-log). I'll attach a short script snippet showing the idempotent delete handler and the cron window.

- Deletion logs: we can produce a redacted sample in JSON lines format with these fields: timestamp_iso, tenant_id_hash, action (DELETE/ERASE), component, initiated_by (api/console/manual), request_id. We'll redact PII and provide a short checksum summary to show integrity.

Note: permanent deletion vs soft-delete — we keep soft-delete markers for up to 7 days (replication & anti-accident window) before hard purge; we'll document the backup retention and explain how our backup retention policy interacts with tenant erasure.

Planning to put the artifacts in a secured share and include a README explaining how to interpret the logs.

Ben Carter
Security Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Lydia Park <lydia.park@finsight.io>
To: ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, ava_chen <ava.chen@redwood.ai>
Cc: LegalOps <legal@finsight.io>, Compliance Team <compliance@finsight.io>
Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 10:15:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Evidence request: retention & deletion - SOC 2 prep

Thanks Ben/Ava — scope clarification: production tenant data only (FinSight account IDs). For the logs, Nov 1–15 window is ideal. For hashed IDs, SHA256 without salt is acceptable for our auditors (they'll treat hashes as pseudonymized).

Requesting:
- residency-retention-matrix.csv (CSV) covering service components and effective TTLs
- audit-log-sample-20261101-20261115.jsonl (redacted JSONL)
- deletion-playbook document describing the soft-delete -> hard-delete timeline and backup retention interactions

Also, can you confirm whether backup snapshots are retained outside of customer region (we need to document cross-region backups for our risk assessment)?

We will need the artifacts by end-of-day Tue 2026-11-30 to meet our internal audit schedule. If you can supply a signed mutual action plan (MAP) indicating delivery commitments, we can attach it to the audit packet.

Best,
Lydia

From: ava_chen <ava.chen@redwood.ai>
To: Lydia Park <lydia.park@finsight.io>
Cc: ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 30 Nov 2026 14:12:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Evidence request: retention & deletion - SOC 2 prep

Lydia — attaching the initial evidence bundle to this message (see attachment stubs). Summary below:

Attachments included:
- residency-retention-matrix.csv — tenant_id_hash, component, primary_region, replication, ttl_days. Rows cover FinSight production services as of 2026-11-15.
- audit-log-sample-20261115.json — redacted JSON lines (tenant_id hashes only), includes request_id and action timestamps.
- deletion-playbook-v2.pdf — explains soft-delete window (7 days), hard purge, backup snapshot TTLs (90 days for incremental snapshots, 365 days for cold backups, see section 2.3).
- ttl-enforcement-script-snippet.sh — shortened snippet showing the idempotent deletion handler and logging calls (for auditor review).

We did a quick check on backups: incremental snapshots used for nearline recovery are replicated to a single secondary region for redundancy; cold archival backups (annual snapshots) may be stored in a different region under customer account controls. We'll add a one-paragraph clarification in the README about cross-region backup storage — Ben will draft.

Links:
- HubSpot record: https://hubspot.com/contacts/HS-2026-9876 (for tracking).
- Jira: https://jira.internal.redwood/SEC-4121 (internal ticket for artifact generation).
- DocuSign MAP: https://www.docusign.com/en/link/abc123-fsa-map (please sign if you want committed delivery dates).

If you want a cryptographic deletion proof (e.g., a hash digest demonstrating object removal from indexes), we can produce a short proposal — we need to align on auditor acceptance.

Ava Chen
Director, Compliance & GTM Security
Redwood Inference

Attachment stubs: residency-retention-matrix.csv (CSV), audit-log-sample-20261115.json (JSONL), deletion-playbook-v2.pdf (PDF), ttl-enforcement-script-snippet.sh (text)

From: Lydia Park <lydia.park@finsight.io>
To: ava_chen <ava.chen@redwood.ai>
Cc: LegalOps <legal@finsight.io>, Compliance Team <compliance@finsight.io>, marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 1 Dec 2026 16:45:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Evidence request: retention & deletion - SOC 2 prep

Ava — received everything, thanks. The audit team opened the JSONL and the CSV and they look consistent. Two quick follow-ups before we close the ticket:

1) For deletion verification our auditors requested a simple deletion-proof proposal: a digest that demonstrates an object id is no longer present in an active index (e.g., Merkle-root of current index with signed timestamp). Would Redwood be open to producing a one-off signed digest for a small set (we'll provide a few hashed IDs)?

2) In deletion-playbook-v2.pdf section 2.3 you mention "cold backups may be stored in a different region under customer account controls" — can you confirm whether FinSight's cold backups are encrypted with keys that the customer controls (KMS) or are managed keys? We need this for our risk scoring.

If you can reply on both items by EOD Fri 2026-12-03, we should be able to finalize the SOC 2 packet. I'll sign the MAP once the DocuSign link is updated to include delivery milestones.

Thanks again — appreciate the quick turnaround.

Lydia
